# Linked Post Strategy Skill

Specialized skill for creating effective Linked Posts on Medium—original content that links to and discusses content published elsewhere.

## What This Skill Does

- **Content Adaptation**: Transform external blog posts into Medium Linked Posts
- **Summary Creation**: Create compelling summaries of original content
- **Value Addition**: Add unique perspective or analysis to Medium audience
- **Cross-Platform Strategy**: Maximize reach across Medium and your own blog
- **Traffic Optimization**: Drive readers between platforms strategically
- **Engagement Building**: Create content that works on both platforms

## Understanding Medium Linked Posts

### What is a Linked Post?

A Linked Post is an article published on Medium that:
- Links to your original content published elsewhere (your blog, Substack, Dev.to, etc.)
- Can be the **exact same article** (if fully cross-posting) or a **summary/curated version**
- Appears in Medium feeds with a "Posted on [external site]" indicator
- Drives traffic to your original content while building Medium audience
- Shows Medium readers "this story was originally posted elsewhere"

### How Linked Posts Appear on Medium

At the top of your article:
```
[Your Name]
Posted on [Your Original Platform]
[Date]
[Share/Bookmark buttons]
```

### Benefits of Linked Posts

✅ **Reach Multiple Audiences**: Medium readers + your blog subscribers
✅ **SEO**: Backlinks from Medium to your site
✅ **Authority**: Establish thought leadership on both platforms
✅ **Traffic**: Drive readers from Medium back to your site
✅ **Discoverability**: Medium's algorithm + your channel
✅ **Less Effort**: One article, two platforms
✅ **Engagement**: Build community on both platforms

## Linked Post Strategy Types

### Strategy 1: Full Cross-Post (100% Identical)
Publish exact same article on both Medium and external site.

**When to use:**
- You want maximum reach on both platforms
- Content is platform-agnostic
- You want Medium's audience to see your work

**Pros:**
- Simple (one article, two places)
- Double the distribution
- Backlink from Medium to your site

**Cons:**
- May not feel "native" to Medium
- Requires same formatting on both
- Comments split between platforms

**Workflow:**
1. Write full article on your platform
2. Format for Medium
3. Publish on Medium as Linked Post
4. Link back to original

---

### Strategy 2: Summary with Original Link (30-50% of Original)
Write a **curated summary** on Medium that links to full article on your site.

**When to use:**
- You want unique Medium content
- Original article is very long
- You want to give Medium exclusive perspective
- Build Medium following, drive clicks to site

**Pros:**
- Unique Medium content
- Teases readers to visit your site
- Better Medium engagement metrics
- Control distribution of traffic

**Cons:**
- More work (write twice)
- Need to maintain consistency
- Readers may prefer Medium's full version

**Workflow:**
1. Write full article on your platform
2. Create **unique** summary for Medium
3. Add exclusive insights/Medium-specific content
4. Link to full article with CTA
5. Publish as Linked Post

---

### Strategy 3: Expansion & Discussion (Original + New Content)
Publish Medium article with original content **plus** curated content and links.

**When to use:**
- You want original Medium content
- Want to reference external sources
- Building thought leadership
- Creating roundups or discussions

**Pros:**
- 100% original Medium content
- More valuable to Medium readers
- Establishes expertise
- Higher engagement

**Cons:**
- Significant effort
- Less direct traffic to original
- Need original Medium-focused content

**Workflow:**
1. Identify topic/sources
2. Create original Medium analysis
3. Include links to sources
4. Add unique perspective/insights
5. Publish as standalone article

---

## Creating an Effective Linked Post (Strategy 2: Recommended)

### Step 1: Choose Your Content
Select articles from your blog that:
- ✅ Perform well on your platform
- ✅ Are technically sound and current
- ✅ Match Medium audience interests
- ✅ Are 1,000+ words (worth summarizing)
- ✅ Have evergreen value (not time-sensitive)

**Avoid:**
- ❌ Very new content (wait 1-2 weeks)
- ❌ Outdated/deprecated content
- ❌ Highly niche/platform-specific
- ❌ Content with broken links

### Step 2: Create Your Medium Summary

**Structure for Linked Post Summary:**

```markdown
# [Attention-Grabbing Title for Medium]

[2-3 sentence intro explaining what readers will learn]

## Key Takeaways
- Point 1: [Insight from original]
- Point 2: [Unique Medium perspective]
- Point 3: [Practical application]

## Main Section 1: [Concept from Your Article]
[1-2 paragraph summary]
[Optional: code snippet if applicable]

## Main Section 2: [Concept from Your Article]
[1-2 paragraph summary]
[Optional: practical example]

## Why This Matters
[Additional context or unique perspective for Medium readers]

## Full Deep Dive
For the complete implementation details, advanced patterns, 
and production examples, read the full article:

**[Full Article Title]** 
[Direct link to original article on your site]
```

### Step 3: Add Medium-Specific Value

To make it a worthwhile Medium article (not just a teaser):

**Add One or More of:**
- 🔍 **New Analysis**: "Here's what this means for Medium readers..."
- 💡 **Additional Examples**: Medium-specific use cases
- 🔗 **Related Resources**: Link to other Medium articles
- ⚠️ **Common Mistakes**: What developers often get wrong
- 🚀 **Advanced Tips**: Ideas not covered in original
- 📊 **Comparison**: How this compares to alternatives

### Step 4: Optimize for Medium

**Title:**
- ❌ Don't just copy original title
- ✅ Adapt for Medium's algorithm
- ✅ Make it benefit-focused
- ✅ Include primary keyword

**Subtitle:**
- Explain what readers gain
- Reference the original platform if it adds credibility
- Example: "A summary of our complete guide to X"

**Tags:**
- Primary topic (e.g., "JavaScript")
- Specific area (e.g., "Performance")
- Related concept (e.g., "Optimization")
- Trend tag (e.g., "DevOps")

### Step 5: Publish as Linked Post

**On Medium:**
1. Click "New story" → "Write a story"
2. Paste/write your content
3. Click "More options" (⋮) near publish
4. Select "This story was originally published elsewhere"
5. Enter your original platform URL
6. Add story metadata (title, subtitle, tags, image)
7. Publish

**Important**: Medium requires you link back to your original. This is what makes it a "Linked Post."

## Content Length Guidelines

**Medium Linked Post (Summary):**
- 800-1,500 words (5-8 min read)
- Extract essential points
- Tease deeper content on original
- Sufficient to stand alone

**Call to Action:**
```markdown
## Ready for More?

This is a summary of [Original Article Title]. 
Read the complete guide on [Your Blog Name]:

[Button/Link to Full Article]

In the full article, you'll discover:
- [Advanced topic 1]
- [Implementation detail 1]
- [Real-world example]
- [Performance benchmark]
```

## Linking Best Practices

### CTA Link Placement
- **End of article**: Primary CTA button
- **Middle section**: Optional secondary link
- **Not too many**: 1-2 links maximum
- **Make it valuable**: "Read the complete implementation..."

### Link Text
```markdown
❌ "Click here"
❌ "Read more"
❌ "Original article"

✅ "Read the complete guide to React Hooks"
✅ "See all advanced optimization techniques"
✅ "View production implementation"
✅ "Discover performance benchmarks"
```

### Link Format on Medium
```markdown
**[Descriptive link text](https://yourdomain.com/article)**

Or use button-style formatting in Medium editor
```

## Publishing Strategy

### Timing

**When to publish Linked Post on Medium:**
- 1-2 weeks after original publication
- Let original content "age" first
- Gives original platform time to gain traction
- Establishes authority before cross-posting

**Frequency:**
- 1 Linked Post every 1-2 weeks (if regular publisher)
- Or every 2-4 weeks for occasional writers
- Don't flood Medium; maintain quality

### Sequencing

**Option 1: Blog First**
1. Publish on your blog (or external platform)
2. Wait 1-2 weeks
3. Create summary + publish on Medium as Linked Post
4. Drive readers back to original

**Option 2: Simultaneous**
1. Publish full article on your platform
2. Same day/next day: Publish summary on Medium
3. Works for timely content
4. Trades off for immediacy

## Measuring Success

### Metrics to Track

**Medium Metrics:**
- ✅ Views on Linked Post
- ✅ Claps/engagement
- ✅ Comments
- ✅ Followers gained
- ✅ Time read

**Blog Metrics:**
- ✅ Clicks from Medium
- ✅ Traffic from Medium referral
- ✅ Avg. session duration
- ✅ Bounce rate
- ✅ Conversions

### What Works Well on Medium for Linked Posts

**High Engagement:**
- Technical how-tos (Linked Posts work great!)
- Comparison/roundup content
- Lessons learned/experience sharing
- Trending technology topics

**Lower Engagement:**
- Overly niche topics
- Purely promotional content
- Outdated information
- Heavy selling (save for CTA)

## SEO Considerations

### Benefits for Your Site
```
Medium article (with backlink)
    ↓
Your original article gets:
- Backlink from established domain
- Referral traffic
- Authority boost
```

### Best Practices

1. **Exact Match**: Use exact URL link in Medium
2. **Anchor Text**: Descriptive (helps SEO)
3. **Not Nofollow**: Medium links are dofollow (unless flagged)
4. **Consistent Domain**: Use same domain/protocol

### URL Structure
```
❌ Don't use: yourdomain.com/article.html?utm_source=medium
✅ Use: yourdomain.com/article

Medium link should match your canonical URL
```

## Frequent Questions & Answers

**Q: Is a Linked Post considered duplicate content?**
A: No. Medium marks it as originally published elsewhere, and you control the canonical. Medium readers see it's a summary, not duplicate.

**Q: Can I use Medium Linked Posts with Substack/Dev.to/etc?**
A: Yes! Medium specifically supports cross-platform publishing. Any platform counts.

**Q: Should I use full article or summary?**
A: Summary works better. It's unique Medium content + drives traffic back to original.

**Q: How many links should I include?**
A: 1-2 maximum. One main CTA at end, optional secondary mid-article.

**Q: Will this hurt my SEO?**
A: No. Proper Linked Post setup with canonical URLs is fine. Medium doesn't penalize.

**Q: How long should I wait before Linked Post?**
A: 1-2 weeks gives original time to gain traction and rankings.

**Q: Can I Linked Post the same article multiple times?**
A: Don't repeat same article. Each Linked Post should be unique content (different summary, different angle, different Medium audience).
